source_text: Tempus est, ut ad alia transeamus; sed reposcit a nobis causae dignitas, ut etiam ea, quae superiore libro putamus praetermissa, reddamus. Quod quidem prudens lector supervacaneum forsitan iudicabit; tamen, quoniam compertum est rerum periculis depositam causam etiam levibus inhaerere, opera est, quibus praesidia sustuleris, auferre solacia.
pass_a_gloss: It is time that we pass to other things; but the dignity of the cause demands from us that we also render those things which in the superior book we think omitted. Which indeed a prudent reader will perhaps judge superfluous; nevertheless, since it has been found that a cause deposited by the dangers of things clings even to light things, it is work to take away the solaces of those from whom you have taken the defenses.
pass_b_english: It is time to move on to other matters. Yet the importance of the case requires us to supply even what we think we passed over in the preceding book. A sensible reader may judge this unnecessary. Still, experience shows that a case brought low by its dangers clings even to slight supports. It is worth taking away the consolations of those whose defenses you have removed.

choices.why: Loaded word in Julian's Latin at this locus; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
